knots.title: InterAgent Framework takes shape
knots.summary: The project starts as the InterAgent Framework in early March 2026, gaining a cross-machine transport layer, an MCP server and a watchdog with retry. Hub packaging fixes and a Docker-served dashboard that configures itself follow, and the first Hub UI improvements land by mid-March.

knots.title: Agent triggers, init wizard and a rapid release cadence
knots.summary: From 19 March the project adds agent triggers and a configurator UI, an interactive init wizard, and Gemini CLI and OpenCode support. A burst of small patch releases follows, along with a migration to stdlib logging, a documentation site and multi-role support for agents.

knots.title: Mission Control, session management and agentweave.yml
knots.summary: Between the end of March and mid-April the Hub gains session-based chat history, a Mission Control UI, an OpenSpec workflow, agent pause/resume and pilot mode. An agentweave.yml config system and Hub setup API arrive, and releases come in quick succession with repeated formatting and compatibility fixes.

knots.title: More runners, shared instructions and a governance framework
knots.summary: From 20 April to early May the project adds agent self-registration, a quality governance framework, OpenCode and Codex runner support, a Linear-style Hub UI redesign and project-wide instructions. It then adds a doctor command, a context builder and diagnostics v2.

knots.title: The 2026 Q2 hardening audit
knots.summary: In June the project runs a structured audit with a 12-PR roadmap. It hardens the transport, the Hub UI authentication and the tests, and merges the audit branch as v0.38.0 / Hub v0.32.0. A Python 3.8 compatibility patch follows as v0.38.1.

knots.title: Native Hub mode, AI-native roles and the spec system
knots.summary: From late June to late July the Hub can run without Docker, with its own PyPI publish workflow. Seven AI-native agent roles are added, the spec skills are overhauled, and a spec role with a Hub Spec tab is introduced. CI moves to OIDC trusted publishing.

knots.title: Version 1.0 and the governed tool surface
knots.summary: Late July to mid-August brings the move to a spec/ root, a unified governed agent tool surface, work on operator-in-the-loop turns, and the fix for an approval defect. Releases 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 follow, then 1.1.0 after an autonomous run that kept a log and a roadmap.

knots.title: The long unreleased stretch: drives, ledgers and spec tooling
knots.summary: After 1.1.0 the project goes unreleased for thousands of commits. The history shows handoff records, live acceptance drives that found new defects, decision sessions recorded in a ledger, overnight iterations on a Codex task, and spec-corpus tooling in the app. By mid-October a re-distilled fact keeps its id.

knots.title: Pull the thread: the idea
knots.summary: On 22 October the Hub's first records appear. Research and two design documents describe a project's whole history as a thread you can pull, backed by a paged chronological feed route and an identity kit source.

knots.title: Building and reviewing the Thread tab
knots.summary: A string of developer, reviewer and QA conversations turn the idea into a working Thread tab. The work covers paged feed wiring, fold-key and actor fixes, knot addressing and link resolution, archived task links, cache-key and bundle merge problems, and Playwright-based acceptance review. A mender frees a task blocked by a dirty checkout.

knots.title: The mender's stranded worktree and the first vault notes
knots.summary: The mender is found stuck on the wrong branch and the operator asks for the files to be committed. Vault notes record the bug, a gap about specs approved after the build, a hard-to-find settings UI, and a request to be notified when an agent replies. The notification request is later recorded as built.

knots.title: Project checks that wait less
knots.summary: Project checks are specified and made to wait for fresh results after master moves. Documents cover what a run does and the path pattern syntax, and a task now shows the spec it came from. Vault notes record the checks going all green, which developer builds a change, and a bug that stops a named reviewer taking the review step.

knots.title: The spec corpus: capability documents
knots.summary: On 23 October the project's specification is adopted into the Hub as a corpus of capability documents. They cover agents and execution, conversations, interface, work and traceability, the vault, runners, loops, checks, spec authoring and governance, task dependencies and usage accounting.

knots.title: The spec corpus: change documents and rulings
knots.summary: Alongside the capabilities, the corpus records many individual rulings and changes. They cover how specs are written and folded, how evidence and reviews decide tasks, how agents, the vault, budgets and costs behave, and how the operator is informed. Each is a small document stating one rule.

knots.title: The thread reads as chapters
knots.summary: A specification makes the manager write the thread as chapters. The chapters store, versioning and migration are built, and the feed shows chapters and knots. The work is reviewed and driven through several QA rounds, including a fix for dropped release tags in the git digest and a check that the feature stays off by default.

knots.title: Finishing the chapters job, tools and UI
knots.summary: On 24 October the chapters manager job is finished and proven. Agent tools for reading and editing chapters and a Thread UI with a weave button are added. Smaller fixes cover the Manager settings, a thread refresh when a job fires, a cache-bearing FR-11 test and black formatting. The page is re-driven against the trial Hub and slice-2 completion is checked.

knots.title: The mender and the stall alarms
knots.summary: Through 24 October the mender is woken again and again for stalled runs, most of them false alarms on live Architect or Developer runs. It closes them, recovers a few dead runs and closes one approved task that skipped its merge. The operator complains about the noise, and a spec says a quiet run is shown to the operator instead.
